source.test: parseModsToml(_:) -- [[mods]] section scan, stops at the next [[ header once modId/displayName found

zipEntries.META-INF/mods.toml:
[[dependencies.jei]]
modId="forge"

[[mods]]
modId = "jei"
displayName = "Just Enough Items"
version = "${file.jarVersion}"

[[mods]]
modId = "decoy"
displayName = "Should Not Be Read"

notes: No MSC 1 test file exercises ModJarMetadataParser/refreshDiscoveredMods directly -- characterized from source (ModJarMetadataParser.swift:133-157, AppViewModel+ModManagement.swift:170-172). The leading [[dependencies.jei]] section is skipped entirely (not '[[mods]]', so in_mods_section stays false while inside it). version = '${file.jarVersion}' is an unresolved Gradle template token, dropped per source's own hasPrefix('${') check -- but refreshDiscoveredMods falls back to the filename heuristic *per field*, not only when the whole manifest read fails ('let version = meta?.version ?? PluginNameParser.extractVersion(from: jarStem)'): meta exists and its modId/displayName are used, but its dropped version still falls through to PluginNameParser on the jar stem, landing on '1.20.1-forge-15.2.0.27' (the stem's own trailing version-looking parts). The second [[mods]] block ('decoy') is never reached -- the scanner stops as soon as it hits the next [[ header while already holding modId/displayName from the first block, matching source's own first-block-only behavior exactly.
